canonical_name: Bernstein inequality (bounded independent summands, upper tail)
canonical_statement: Let X_0,...,X_(n-1) be mutually independent centered real random variables on a probability space. If |X_i| <= b almost surely, b >= 0, v >= 0, and the sum of their variances is at most v, then for every t >= 0, P(sum_i X_i >= t) <= exp(-t^2 / (2*(v + b*t/3))).
domain_and_universes: Omega : Type u with MeasurableSpace Omega; a probability measure mu; n : Nat; X : Nat -> Omega -> Real; b v t : Real; proposition in Lean universe 0
ordered_binders: problem package (mu, n, X, v, b and hypotheses)
hypotheses: X_i is a.e.-measurable for i < n
X_i belongs to L2 for i < n
the family X is mutually independent
integral X_i dmu = 0 for i < n
|X_i| <= b almost everywhere for i < n
sum over i < n of Var(X_i; mu) <= v
conclusion: mu.real {omega | t <= sum over i < n of X_i omega} <= exp (-(t^2) / (2*(v + b*t/3)))
excluded_variants: unbounded summands satisfying only moment or sub-exponential conditions
